title: Mexican cultural participation rebounds but remains stratified by age, education, identity, time, cost, and digital form
source_unit: INEGI Módulo sobre Eventos Culturales Seleccionados, MODECULT 2025

observations.period: June 2025; selected cultural-event attendance, comparable adult series

denominator.unit: sampled dwellings in MODECULT 2025; comparable 2016-2025 series reports population aged 18+ in 32 cities of 100,000+ inhabitants

adults_attending_selected_cultural_event.unit: percent of population aged 18+; theatre, live music, dance, exhibition, or cinema in previous 12 months
percent of population aged 18+ in comparable series
percent of population aged 18+ in comparable series

observations.method: INEGI MODECULT 2025 direct interviews using a probabilistic, stratified, four-stage sample of 4,818 dwellings, with national, urban/rural, and 32-city coverage; the 18+ series is retained separately from the new 12+ indicators.
observations.uncertainty: The comparable series covers 32 urban areas and selected event types, not all cultural practices or the full national population. Year-to-year changes can reflect post-pandemic normalization, event supply, prices, and survey redesign; attendance is not frequency, quality, or cultural meaning.
observations.subgroup: Population aged 18+ in the 32 cities of 100,000+ inhabitants for the comparable series; the 2025 redesign additionally reports population aged 12+ nationally.
observations.counterinterpretation: The 2025 rebound does not restore the 2016 attendance rate in the comparable series; recovery can coexist with a changed event mix, unequal access, and more digitally mediated participation.

denominator.unit: sampled dwellings; national estimates for population aged 12+ are survey-weighted

basic_incomplete_attendance.unit: percent among population with incomplete basic education

higher_education_attendance.unit: percent among population with higher education

observations.method: INEGI MODECULT 2025 cross-tabulations of cultural attendance by age, sex, education, self-identification/language, and disability status; the source reports percentages rather than causal effects.
observations.uncertainty: Subgroup percentages have different effective sample sizes and may have sampling error; the release does not establish why groups differ. Identity, education, age, disability, income, geography, transport, event supply, and time are correlated.
observations.subgroup: Mexican population aged 12+ at national level, disaggregated by age, sex, education, Afrodescendant identity, Indigenous self-identification, Indigenous-language status, and disability.
observations.counterinterpretation: The near gender parity should not be read as equal access: age, education, language, and disability gradients are much larger, and higher attendance may reflect urban access, school exposure, income, or event preferences rather than cultural inclusion alone.

observations.period: June 2025; cultural barriers, artistic participation, and online cultural consumption

denominator.unit: Event-specific non-attenders; artistic participants aged 12+; women aged 12+ who viewed cultural events online; all people aged 12+ for organizing. Numeric subgroup bases are not supplied.

population_12plus_acting_in_theater.unit: percent among those reporting artistic activities; activity-specific distribution

population_12plus_dancing.unit: percent among those reporting artistic activities; activity-specific distribution

population_12plus_audio_visual_creation.unit: percent among those reporting artistic activities; activity-specific distribution

women_online_cultural_viewers_watching_l.unit: percent of women aged 12+ who viewed cultural events online

women_online_cultural_viewers_watching_c.unit: percent of women aged 12+ who viewed cultural events online

observations.method: MODECULT 2025 expanded its questionnaire to collect reasons for non-attendance, artistic activity, cultural-event organization/support, and virtual cultural attendance. The reported percentages use activity- or event-specific conditional denominators. Charts visually checked on PDF pages 22, 23, 26 and 28: dance barriers, conditional artistic activity, national organizing, and women-specific online viewing.
observations.uncertainty: Barrier categories are self-reported and mutually structured within event-specific non-attender populations; they do not prove that cost, time, supply, or interest caused non-attendance. Online viewing percentages do not measure duration, payment, platform, or substitution for in-person attendance.
observations.subgroup: Mexican population aged 12+; event-specific non-attenders, artistic participants, online cultural consumers, and cultural-event organizers/supporters.
observations.counterinterpretation: Activity mix among artistic participants and online viewers cannot establish population-wide prevalence or be directly compared with the national organizer share.

related_sources.claim: INEGI's official MODECULT program page documents the 2025 conceptual redesign, objectives, population, coverage, sample, periodicity, and historical comparability boundary.
INEGI's official metadata catalog documents MODECULT 2025's sample design, population, concepts, and data materials.
The prior MODECULT 2024 presentation supplies the immediately preceding comparable adult attendance estimate used in the 2016-2025 series.

boundary: This record adds direct cultural participation, barrier, artistic-agency, organizer, and online-consumption evidence to the Mexico household-spending and Brazil/Canada retail layers. The comparable 2016-2025 adult series covers 32 large urban areas, while the redesigned 2025 indicators cover people aged 12+ nationally; these universes must not be merged. The record does not measure cultural quality, identity formation, causal access barriers, spending amounts, or long-run social outcomes. Source-dependence audit 2026-09-30: the companion MODECULT 2025 record uses the same survey wave; overlapping estimates are not independent corroboration.
